messages:
todd: Heads-up — I opened a tiny TF change to add an ephemeral GPU nodepool for short-lived batch inference (burst capacity). It's targetting spot first, with a small capacity-reserve fallback. Can people eyeball the config? thinking about instance types + preempt handling.

jen: link pls to the PR? Also want to check secrets/user-data wiring for the bootstrap script (we can't leak creds to spot instances).

infra-bot: PR #4127: terraform: add ephemeral-gpu-pool (plan attached) — 3 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. CI: terraform-init/plan passed.

jen: thanks. quick skim — curious about this block in modules/gpu_pool/main.tf:```hcl
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "ephemeral_gpu" {
  name_prefix = "ephemeral-gpu-"
  mixed_instances_policy {
    instances_distribution {
      on_demand_allocation_strategy = "prioritized"
      spot_allocation_strategy = "capacity-optimized"
      on_demand_base_capacity = 0
      on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 0
    }
    launch_template {
      launch_template_specification {
        launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id
      }
      overrides = [
        { instance_type = "p5.24xlarge" },
        { instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge" }
      ]
    }
  }
  desired_capacity = var.desired_capacity
  min_size = 0
  max_size = var.max_size
}
```
jen: what ensures we don't attach the KMS keys/secrets directly to spot user-data? we need the instance role to fetch secrets from Secrets Manager and the user-data to only pull ephemeral tokens.

maria: agree. In the LT I added `iam_instance_profile = aws_iam_instance_profile.ephemeral_gpu.name` and the role has a narrow policy to read "/redwood/ephemeral-node-bootstrap/*" from SM. Boot script pulls a short-lived token from the instance metadata, then uses STS to assume `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ephemeral-bootstrap-role` which has a limited time window. No long-lived creds in user-data.

jen: ok good. can you paste the user-data snippet?

maria: ```bash
#!/bin/bash
# minimal bootstrap
TOKEN=$(curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/role-name)
# assume role flow, then fetch secret
aws sts assume-role --role-arn $ASSUME_ROLE_ARN --role-session-name bootstrap > /tmp/creds.json
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(jq -r .Credentials.AccessKeyId /tmp/creds.json)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(jq -r .Credentials.SecretAccessKey /tmp/creds.json)
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(jq -r .Credentials.SessionToken /tmp/creds.json)
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id /redwood/ephemeral-node-bootstrap/kubeconfig --query SecretString --output text > /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.yaml
# join cluster etc.
```

maria: note: the assume-role ARN is injected by LT tag via SSM parameter — no secrets in TF state.

jen: nice. two ops-questions: 1) eviction policy if spot is reclaimed — do we drain gracefully? 2) capacity reservation fallback: how is that wired?

maria: eviction handling: we run a small daemonset on those nodes that listens for EC2 Spot interruption notices (IMDS webhook) and triggers `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. We also set `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` in the pods to 120s for batch jobs.

maria: capacity reservation: TF creates an `aws_capacity_reservation` resource per AZ with `instance_type = var.preferred_instance` but it's only created when `var.reserve_capacity = true`. For ephemeral default we keep `reserve_capacity = false` and allow autoscaling to pick up on-demand when spot not available.

jen: ok, that's reasonable. For the node labels/taints — we should make sure schedulers can preempt lower-priority work. Add: `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu-ephemeral` and taint `gpu-ephemeral=true:NoSchedule`. Then pods opt-in via tolerations.

maria: added in `aws_launch_template` user-data tags + kubelet extraArgs: `--node-labels=node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=gpu-ephemeral` and a systemd unit applies the taint on boot. Snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: example-batch
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-ephemeral"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: gpu-ephemeral
  containers:
  - name: run
    image: ...
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

todd: pinging @jen — do you want to block this for a short security review, or is it safe to merge and monitor? We need burst pool for the weekend jobs.

jen: I'm +1 to merge after a quick checklist: verify IAM policy scoping, ensure SSM param doesn't contain sensitive data, and confirm infra-bot plan output is archived in the PR. Also run a dry deploy to staging.

sre-oncall: add one more thing — update the node termination doc with `kubectl drain` behavior and who gets paged. If batch jobs run longer than 2m we should gate them behind a job controller that can checkpoint.

todd: will do. I'll add the checklist to the PR and kick off a staging deploy now. If CI passes and jen OKs, I'll merge and watch the canary. :eyes:

infra-bot: terraform apply queued by todd for workspace `staging` — plan applied to staging at 2032110300.

jen: thanks. leave a note here when staging nodes come up so I can spot-check kubelet logs and IAM get-secret calls.

maria: staging up at 2032110400 — two nodes in us-west-2a with p5.24xlarge, user-data fetched secrets successfully. kubelet logs look clean.

todd: merging to main in 30m if no further issues. thanks all :thumbsup:
